items.prompt: What does the title suggest the chart is about?

how to find a job in Australia

exercises.title: Complete the flow-chart (Ex. 4)
exercises.instruction: Read the short text and then complete the flow-chart using ONE WORD ONLY from the text.

stimulus.text:
Studying abroad

Studying abroad as an international student can be an enriching experience. If you have a good level of English, you will face the difficult decision of deciding which university you would like to apply to. Once you have chosen, you can contact the university directly in order to apply.

In order to successfully obtain a place at university, you will need to get a visa to study at the university of your choice. In order to obtain a visa, you will need proof of admission to the college. You will also need to show that you have enough funds for the first year of study. After you have done this, you can apply for a visa. Once you have received a visa, you can start to look for flights and also try to find somewhere to live. This is something that you don't need to worry about, as each university has an accommodation team to help you. Furthermore, preferential treatment is given for new students from abroad.
stimulus.caption: Studying abroad (p. 129)

items.prompt: Step 1 – Choose a university and enrol: Once you have chosen, you can apply ____ to the university for a place.
items.explanation: "you can contact the university **directly** in order to apply".

items.prompt: Step 2 – Apply for a student visa: Once you have confirmation of ____ and adequate ____ for the first year, you can apply for your visa.
items.explanation: "you will need proof of **admission**… enough **funds** for the first year".

items.prompt: Step 3 – Book your flight and accommodation: each university has an accommodation team that can help you find a place, especially for ____ students.
items.explanation: "preferential treatment is given for **new** students from abroad".

exercises.title: How were the words explained? (Ex. 16–17)
exercises.instruction: How were these words explained in the texts: by footnote, an explanation in the text, or an explanation given by the surrounding context?

stimulus.text:
How the modern computer works

The mouse and keyboard are input units: ways of getting information into your computer. Most computers store all this information on a hard drive (a huge magnetic memory). However, smaller computer-based devices like digital cameras and mobile phones use other kinds of storage, such as flash memory cards.

The computer's processor, also known as the central processing unit, is a microchip* buried deep inside. As it is used it becomes incredibly hot and a fan prevents the computer from overheating.

Many computers now have LCD screens, capable of displaying high-resolution graphics, such as very clear and detailed photographs. Many computers also have loudspeakers and can be connected to a printer.

*microchip – a very small part of a computer or machine that does calculations or stores information
stimulus.caption: How the modern computer works (p. 133)

items.explanation: "a piece of cloth with ink on it called the ribbon".
"other kinds of storage, such as flash memory cards".
"such as very clear and detailed photographs".
